private.ask: Where is your data? Who can read it?
private.where1: In your own space, separate from everyone else’s, on a server in the European Union (OVHcloud or Hetzner). Or on your own computer, if you install it at home.
private.where2: With All included, an encrypted backup every hour, with a key only your devices hold: we keep it without being able to read it.
private.where3: It’s all yours: you can take everything and leave whenever you like.
private.who1: Not us: Kerfy Studio doesn’t read your conversations and trains no AI with them. No ads, no tracking.
private.who2: The AI reads what your agent sends it, to answer you: through EUrouter, a European AI router, then the company running the model you chose. The app names them before your first message.
private.who3: Our limit, said plainly: as with any rented server, the host and we could technically get in. Our software doesn’t, and we only would if the law required it.

1.a: Your own AI agents, the Bips, in the app on iPhone, iPad and Android. They work in your own space, on a server in Europe that we look after: nothing to install, nothing to set up, updates and backups included.

2.a: Often: a week to start, while there are some left this month and if you never had one. We tell you before you pay whether it applies, when it ends and the price that follows. Stop before it ends and nothing is charged.

3.a: Each plan has its AI credit for the month: €0.50 for Solo, €1 for Duo, €3 for Family, shared by everyone in it. The app shows it as an estimated number of messages with your model: a simple exchange counts as one, a task in the browser for much more (often several dozen). In Duo and Family, the person who pays sees how much each person uses, never what they write, and can set a limit per person. What’s left carries over to the next month. Need more: extra credit in the app, and it never expires. Out of credit: the agents take a break until next month, nothing is lost.

4.a: Not us: Kerfy Studio doesn’t read them or train any AI on them. To answer you, the AI reads what your agent sends it: through EUrouter, a European AI router, then the company running the chosen model, which the app names before your first message. As we rent the server, we could technically enter your space: our software doesn’t, and we only would if the law required it.

5.q: How do Duo and Family work?
5.a: Each invited person has their own account, space and agents; the plan’s AI credit is shared. Neither the person who pays nor we read anyone else’s conversations: the person who pays only sees how much credit each person uses. With Family, up to six people share a server that’s yours alone.

6.q: Can I stop whenever I want?
6.a: Yes, at no cost: the subscription ends at the end of the paid period. Your space is then kept for 30 days so you can take everything with you, then erased with its backups. And you have 14 days to change your mind after buying.

7.q: Why is it cheaper on the web?
7.a: In the app, the App Store and Google Play take a commission. On the web it’s smaller, so we pass it on to you. Same service: you sign in to the app with the same account.

8.a: Both, and iPad too: iOS 18 or later, Android 10 or later. In English, French, German and Spanish.

9.a: Nous Research’s open-source AI agent. BipAgents is an independent app built on it: it turns your Hermes agents into Bips you take everywhere.

10.a: The app is free: one command installs it on your computer or server, and you only pay for the AI model you pick. The subscription spares you all that.

11.q: Which AI model, and is it any good?
11.a: GLM-5.3 Flash by default. You can pick another one in the app, such as DeepSeek, with its price shown. For everyday tasks (email, calendar, searches, bookings), it comes very close to the top models. A more powerful model uses up your AI credit faster. Before your first message, the app names the router and the model’s maker. On your own computer, you bring the model of your choice.

family.title: In a family, your agents talk to each other.
family.sub: Everyone keeps their own private space and agents. When what you tell your agent concerns someone in the family, it offers to pass it on to their agent: you read it, you choose who gets it, and nothing leaves until you tap “Send”.
family.s1: You tell your agent: it offers to let Sam know. You read it, you send it; Sam is told and Sam’s agent knows.
family.s2: You booked 12 to 19 August: your agent offers to give the dates to the whole family, and every agent has them.
family.s3: “I’m ordering lunch today”: your agent asks whether to tell the others. One “No thanks”, and it won’t bring it up again.
family.p1: The words and the recipients can be changed before sending
family.p2: Left unanswered, a proposal goes away after a day
family.p3: Your own agents write to each other and pass files only where you allowed it: “Who can write to whom”
family.p4: Family: up to 6 people, each with their own space, and a shared AI credit
family.a11y: In the conversation, the Daily agent offers: let Sam know? The words “The school called: Léa has a fever, I’m picking her up”, Sam as the recipient, and the Send and No thanks buttons. At Sam’s, the notification arrives.
